geocode_endpoint.description: Open-Meteo geocoding endpoint, queried as GET <endpoint>?name=<place>&count=1&language=<lang> (WEATHER_GEOCODE_ENDPOINT)

forecast_endpoint.description: Open-Meteo forecast endpoint, queried as GET <endpoint>?latitude=..&longitude=..&daily=..&current=.. (WEATHER_FORECAST_ENDPOINT)

user_agent.description: The User-Agent both requests carry: a free service is told who calls it

default_language.description: The language of place names and condition words when the call names none (`en` and `de` have condition words; any other language reads English words)

now_utc.description: Test override of the `fetched_at` stamp (ISO 8601, UTC). Empty = the wall clock of the call

condition_lang.description: Language data: per language the WMO weather-code words (`codes`) and the phrases of the spoken summary (`phrases`: now, day, today, tomorrow, unknown). A language without a table reads English

description.purpose: The `weather` occupant of the tools hive (GH #1260): the forecast of one named place from Open-Meteo, a free service without a key -- so no grant, no credential lane and nothing in `.env` beyond two optional endpoints. Two GETs: the geocoder resolves the place, the forecast answers for its coordinates.
description.use_when: Reached on hop.tool_name == 'weather' inside a tools hive. It is the quick path's tool for a weather question: the answer is meant to be spoken as it comes.
description.not_in_scope: No history, no alerts, no hourly series and no unit choice (Celsius, millimetres). No ranking of places either: the geocoder's first hit is the place, and its country is named in the answer so a wrong town is audible.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: ONE tool_result turn whose text is a JSON object -- `summary` (one sentence that can be spoken as it is), `place` {name, country, admin1, latitude, longitude}, `timezone`, `current` {time, temp, weather_code, condition}, `days` [{date, temp_min, temp_max, precipitation_mm, weather_code, condition}], `fetched_at` (UTC) and `source`. hop.operation is always `weather`. A refusal is an ordinary result too: its text is {error, error_code} and hop.error_code names it -- `invalid_input` (no `place`, or `days` outside 1..7), `place_not_found` (the geocoder knows no such place), `timeout` (the service did not answer within external_timeout_ms), `io_error` (no connection) or `upstream_error` (a non-2xx answer or no JSON).
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the tool_call turn; its text is the arguments {place, days?, language?}.
examples: {place: 'Berlin', language: 'en'} -> tool_result {summary: 'Berlin, Germany: now 13 °C, overcast; today 9 °C to 15 °C, light rain, 2.1 mm precipitation.', days: [...]}
{place: 'Atlantis'} -> tool_result {error: 'no place named Atlantis was found', error_code: 'place_not_found'}, hop {error_code: 'place_not_found'}
